samples.prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for everyone, while others think students should pay for it. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
text: Whether higher education should be funded by the state or by students is a question that divides governments and families alike. While free tuition promotes equality, I believe a carefully designed system of shared costs is more sustainable.

Those in favour of free university education make a powerful argument based on fairness. If tuition is charged, talented students from poor families may abandon their ambitions or graduate with debts that shape their careers for decades. Free access, by contrast, treats education as a public good, much like healthcare, and allows society to benefit from the skills of everyone who is capable of study. Countries such as Finland, which charge no fees, also tend to enjoy high levels of social mobility.

However, opponents of the idea raise a legitimate concern about cost. Universities are expensive to run, and when the entire bill falls on taxpayers, funding is often squeezed, resulting in overcrowded lecture halls and outdated laboratories. Moreover, graduates typically earn more than non-graduates, so it can seem unfair to ask a nurse or a builder to subsidise the future income of a lawyer.

In my view, the best solution lies between these extremes. Fees should be modest, and repayment should depend on a graduate’s later income, so that no one is prevented from studying by lack of money. Grants for the poorest students would complete the system. This approach protects both access and quality.
In conclusion, although free university education is an attractive ideal, a balanced model in which the state and graduates share the cost is likely to be fairer and more effective in the long run.
notes: Kirish savolni o‘z so‘zlari bilan qayta aytadi va aniq pozitsiya (tezis) beradi.
Har bir paragraf bitta g‘oya: 1) tarafdorlar, 2) qarshilar, 3) o‘z fikri. Har g‘oya sabab va misol bilan ochilgan.
Bog‘lovchilar tabiiy: however, moreover, by contrast, in conclusion (har gapga emas).
So‘z boyligi: public good, social mobility, legitimate concern, subsidise — aniq birikmalar.
Grammatika xilma-xil: nisbiy gap (which charge no fees), shart gap (If tuition is charged…), passiv, ravishdosh (resulting in…).

samples.prompt: Many people believe that children should start learning a foreign language at primary school. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
text: It is increasingly common for primary schools to introduce a foreign language. Although this policy has some drawbacks, I believe the advantages are considerably greater.

The most important benefit is that young children learn languages with remarkable ease. Before puberty, the brain is highly receptive to new sounds, which helps pupils acquire natural pronunciation that adults rarely achieve. Furthermore, an early start gives students many more years of practice, so they are likely to reach a higher level of fluency by the time they leave school. Learning another language also encourages curiosity about other cultures, a quality that is valuable in an interconnected world.

There are, nevertheless, some disadvantages. The primary curriculum is already crowded, and time spent on a language may reduce lessons in reading, mathematics or science. In addition, many primary teachers are not trained language specialists, and poor teaching at an early age could discourage children rather than inspire them.

However, these problems can be solved. Language lessons can be short and playful, based on songs and games rather than grammar, so that they take up little time while keeping children motivated. Governments can also invest in teacher training, or use specialist teachers who travel between schools.

In conclusion, the main obstacles are practical rather than fundamental. Since early learners gain better pronunciation, more practice time and broader cultural awareness, I firmly believe that the benefits of teaching foreign languages in primary schools outweigh the drawbacks.
notes: ‘Outweigh’ savolida pozitsiya boshidan aniq: afzalliklar ko‘proq.
Tuzilma: afzalliklar → kamchiliklar → ularning yechimi → xulosa. Yechimlar paragrafi inshoni chuqurlashtiradi.
Har g‘oya sabab bilan: ‘brain is highly receptive’ → ‘natural pronunciation’.
Collocations: remarkable ease, crowded curriculum, practical rather than fundamental, firmly believe.
Xulosa yangi g‘oya qo‘shmaydi, tezisni boshqacha so‘zlar bilan takrorlaydi.
